LESSON: HUMAN CIRCULATORY SYSTEM

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: IMPAIRMENT SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Living things and the Environment
Topic 1.3: Human Circulatory system
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Human Circulatory system, part of Living things and the Environment in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six IMPAIRMENT SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: How does blood circulate in the body? 2. Why is blood important to the body?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Human Circulatory system together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-Efficacy: The learner is aware of their needs therefore successfully designs a criterion for maintaining a healthy

circulatory system.

• Digital literacy - interacting with digital technology: The learner uses new digital technology such as simulation software,

online interactive platforms or digital images to illustrate the human circulatory system.

• Learning to learn - independent learning: The learner independently interacts with digital technology and successfully

searches for information on the layout of the human circulatory system and common conditions of the human circulatory

system

Values:
• Responsibility - accountability: The learner observes safety precautions by showing resilience and consistency in

practicing ways for maintaining a healthy circulatory system.

• Unity- equality: The learner embraces others by respecting their opinions as they collaboratively discuss ways of

maintaining a healthy human circulatory system.

PCIs:

Health promotion issues- Prevention of non-communicable diseases: Learner adopts a routine for maintaining a healthy

circulatory system.

14

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: How does blood circulate in the body? 2. Why is blood important to the body?
